standard_prerequisites.name: The characterization of quasi-compactness by the existence of an affine open whose preimage is not quasi-compact, cited from the schemes chapter
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cited at proof lines 9995-9997 and again at 10011-10013
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the affine base to work over and the bad point at which every neighbourhood has non-quasi-compact preimage.

standard_prerequisites.name: The description of points of a fibre product by a pair of points together with a prime in the tensor product of their residue fields, cited from the schemes chapter
standard_prerequisites.use: Allows the point constructed over a chosen point of X and a chosen point of the auxiliary affine space to be lifted to the fibre product.

standard_prerequisites.name: The description of the closed subscheme cut out by a family of coordinate functions as a polynomial algebra on the remaining coordinates, and the bijection between its points over a given base point and the spectrum of the same polynomial algebra over that residue field
standard_prerequisites.use: Makes it possible to choose the auxiliary point avoiding the zero locus of a prescribed polynomial while lying in the vanishing loci of the omitted coordinates.

core_obligations: Reduce to an affine base: argue by contraposition, so assume the morphism is not quasi-compact, find an affine open of the base whose preimage is not quasi-compact, and replace the base by that affine open (proof lines 9993-10000).

Set up the auxiliary affine space: write the source as a union of affine opens, form the affine space over the base with one coordinate for each member of the family, remove from the fibre product the union of the pieces cut out by the corresponding coordinate being nonzero, and observe that it suffices to show the image of that closed set under the projection to the auxiliary space is not closed (proof lines 10002-10007).

Choose a bad point of the base: there is a point with no neighbourhood over which the source becomes quasi-compact, since otherwise finitely many such neighbourhoods would make the morphism quasi-compact (proof lines 10009-10014).

Identify a point missing the image on one fibre: over that bad point take the point of the auxiliary space with all coordinates equal to one and residue field that of the base point; it lies in every piece, and the fibre of the closed set over it is empty, so it escapes the image on that fibre (proof lines 10016-10023).

Contradiction: if the image were closed, a polynomial vanishing on it but not at that point has a coefficient nonzero at the base point, hence invertible on a neighbourhood; taking the finite set of coordinates occurring in that polynomial and using non-quasi-compactness over the neighbourhood produces a point of the source avoiding the corresponding affine opens, and the invertibility of the coefficient produces a point of the auxiliary space over the same base point avoiding the polynomial's zero locus while vanishing on the omitted coordinates; the fibre product point lift then lies in the closed set but its image avoids the zero locus, a contradiction (proof lines 10025-10047).
proof_roadmap: Argue by contraposition over an affine base and encode the failure of quasi-compactness by an auxiliary affine space with one coordinate per affine chart of the source (proof lines 9993-10014).

Find a point over a bad point of the base that escapes the image on that fibre, then exploit a polynomial vanishing on the image together with the invertibility of one of its coefficients to construct a point of the closed set whose image escapes the zero locus (proof lines 10016-10047).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that a universally closed morphism of schemes is quasi-compact, so that universal closedness cannot hold for a morphism that fails to be quasi-compact (statement lines 9985-9991). The counted proof is a contrapositive argument of real substance: after reducing to an affine base it builds an auxiliary affine space with one coordinate per affine chart of the source, cuts out a closed subset of the fibre product encoding the failure of the charts to cover, produces a point over a strategically chosen bad point of the base that escapes the image on that fibre, and then uses a polynomial vanishing on the image together with the invertibility of one coefficient to construct a point of the closed subset whose image avoids the zero locus of that polynomial, contradicting closedness (proof lines 9993-10047). It is H2: every step is carried out in the counted span and the cited inputs are standard criteria for quasi-compactness and for points of fibre products.
